summary.intent: Add a real street map underlay behind the existing SVG route line on the tedlasso-strava activity page, since a bare path shape wasn't as helpful as seeing the route on a city map.
summary.outcome: Implemented a full basemap feature: a pure Web Mercator projection module (basemap.ts), a same-origin tile proxy (tiles.ts) to avoid leaking visitor data to the tile host, newsprint-styled tile rendering with dark-mode inversion, a scale bar, a BASEMAP=off kill switch, 60 new tests (371 total passing, 97.3% branch coverage), visual verification via headless Chrome screenshots in both themes, updated docs (CLAUDE.md, spec decision log, README), and committed everything to a new branch feat/route-basemap without pushing.

repo: Two route path coordinate systems coexist and must never be mixed: RouteRender.pathD is equirectangular normalized into an abstract 1000x1000 box, while basemap.pathD is Web Mercator in tile pixels aligned to the actual map tiles

The original spec explicitly chose inline SVG over tile providers to avoid leaking visitor IPs to a third party; reversing that decision required proxying tiles server-side (one Worker request instead of per-visitor) to preserve the original privacy guarantee

Route privacy trimming happens in the write path before persistence (DEFAULT_PRIVACY_TRIM_M); the basemap must be built only from already-redacted segments so nothing untrimmed is ever persisted or rendered

CARTO Positron tiles sit in the top 6% of the tonal range (streets ~#f2f2f2 on white), so a plain opacity fade erases them — a levels stretch (brightness→contrast→brightness) plus mix-blend-mode:multiply is needed to make them read as printed on newsprint stock

Snapshots written before a schema change (basemap field) must be handled as optional/nullable and fall back gracefully — KV-stored snapshots are a trust boundary and untrusted JSON, so numeric coercion (NaN→0) and HTML escaping are required for all snapshot-derived render values
The Cache API only accepts GET requests, so tile proxy caching must skip HEAD requests and go straight upstream
Vitest coverage gate in this repo is 95% branches; project uses npm run typecheck, npm test, npm run coverage as verification commands

code.finding: New pure domain module computing fit zoom, tile grid layout, Web Mercator re-projection of route segments, and a scale bar; must return null when coordinates are non-finite or every segment is a single stranded point

Tile proxy route handler: bounds-checks z/x/y, uses edge cache (skipping non-GET), serves a transparent 1x1 PNG fallback on upstream failure so a bad minute degrades gracefully instead of showing broken images

renderRoute now takes a showBasemap param (defaults true); mapFrame() renders tile layers plus a doubled-stroke SVG line (stock-colored casing under ink-accent) so the route stays visible crossing street labels; all snapshot-derived numeric/string fields pass through defensive coercion (n()) and escapeHtml()

Added resolveBasemap(env.BASEMAP) exported function: opt-out via case-insensitive 'off' literal only, checked at render time (not bake-time) so toggling takes effect on next page view without a re-fetch; /tiles/ routes are checked first in the fetch handler for performance since there are ~15-20 per page view

BASEMAP_WIDTH/HEIGHT/PADDING and BASEMAP_MIN_ZOOM(3)/MAX_ZOOM(16) constants added; zoom floor avoids continent-level tiles, ceiling avoids exceeding street-level detail where trimmed routes stop fitting

workflow: Used a scratchpad directory with an esbuild-bundled preview-server.ts plus headless Chrome screenshots to visually verify CSS/rendering changes before committing, since this is a Cloudflare Worker app without an easy live-reload UI test path

Iteratively tuned tile color-processing filters (brightness/contrast values) by generating multiple composited PNG variants with PIL and visually inspecting them before picking final CSS filter values
Wrote tests asserting scale-bar accuracy against real haversine ground-truth distance rather than just checking the label renders
Used python3 heredoc scripts via Bash for precise multi-file string-replacement edits instead of the Edit tool in several places
Deliberately excluded untracked .claude/.codex/.entire tooling directories from the commit as unrelated to the feature

friction: Had to reinstall node_modules mid-session for coverage to run
Initial preview-server.ts had hardcoded absolute paths that needed correcting before it would run
First screenshot review revealed scale bar/positioning issues requiring CSS iteration (padding assumptions were wrong, scale bar background handling needed fixing)
Needed multiple rounds of pole-wrapping edge case fixes in basemap tests (north pole, south pole, antimeridian) to get coverage gate passing

Reversing a previously deliberate architectural decision (spec explicitly rejected tile providers) required careful documentation to justify why the new approach doesn't reintroduce the original privacy concern
